citation: Fox MC, Ericsson KA, Best R. Do procedures for verbal reporting of thinking have to be reactive? Psychological Bulletin. 2011;137(2):316-344. doi:10.1037/a0021663
notes: Simple concurrent think-aloud effect on accuracy ~zero; directed explaining/describing is reactive; all verbal procedures increase completion time.

citation: Schön DA. Designing as reflective conversation with the materials of a design situation. Knowledge-Based Systems. 1992;5(1):3-14. doi:10.1016/0950-7051(92)90020-G

citation: Clemmensen T, Hertzum M, Hornbæk K, Shi Q, Yammiyavar P. Cultural cognition in usability evaluation. Interacting with Computers. 2009;21(3):212-220. doi:10.1016/j.intcom.2009.05.003
source_type: conceptual synthesis grounded in prior empirical work
notes: Useful boundary evidence; its East/West framing is itself coarse and must not be promoted as a causal country rule.

citation: A Panoramic View of Socio-Cultural Sensitivity in Digital Technologies: A Comprehensive Review and Future Directions. International Journal of Human-Computer Interaction. 2024. doi:10.1080/10447318.2024.2372135
notes: Supports context/community-value sensitivity; does not justify national stereotypes.

citation: Palmer SE. Common region: A new principle of perceptual grouping. Cognitive Psychology. 1992;24(3):436-447. doi:10.1016/0010-0285(92)90014-S
culture_axes: low direct culture relevance; visual organization
notes: Common region strongly affects grouping and can overcome proximity/similarity; supports separating grouping from quantity.

citation: Reinecke K, Gajos KZ. Quantifying Visual Preferences Around the World. CHI 2014:11-20.
culture_axes: country; gender; education; visual complexity; colorfulness
notes: Peak appeal for complexity/colorfulness varies strongly with participant background; direct evidence against universal aesthetic preference settings.

citation: Lavie T, Tractinsky N. Assessing dimensions of perceived visual aesthetics of web sites. International Journal of Human-Computer Studies. 2004;60(3):269-298. doi:10.1016/j.ijhcs.2003.09.002
culture_axes: original study context not culturally broad
notes: Distinguishes classical/order-clear aesthetics from expressive/creative-original aesthetics.

citation: Tractinsky N, Katz AS, Ikar D. What is beautiful is usable. Interacting with Computers. 2000;13(2):127-145. doi:10.1016/S0953-5438(00)00031-X
notes: Found strong aesthetics-perceived-usability relationship; retained as support for coupling, not causal universality.

citation: Tuch AN, Roth SP, Hornbæk K, Opwis K, Bargas-Avila JA. Is beautiful really usable? Computers in Human Behavior. 2012;28(5):1596-1607. doi:10.1016/j.chb.2012.03.024

citation: Khashman N. Arabic web interface design through the eyes of Hofstede. ASIS&T Proceedings. 2012/2013. doi:10.1002/meet.14504901369
population_or_context: 100 ministry web interfaces across 10 Arab countries
notes: Hofstede-derived predictions did not fully reflect observed interface characteristics; evidence against treating Arab countries as a single deterministic design culture.

citation: Chen CH, Li S. The effect of visual feedback types on the wait indicator interface of a mobile application. Displays. 2019. doi:10.1016/j.displa.2019.101928
notes: Feedback type and wait duration changed perceived time/evaluation; one feedback type reduced perceived waiting without universally improving experience.

citation: W3C WAI. Understanding Success Criterion 4.1.3: Status Messages. Updated 2026.
notes: Separates success/result, waiting, progress and errors as status information; warns excessive alerts can make interfaces too chatty.

citation: W3C WAI. G199: Providing success feedback when data is submitted successfully.
notes: Explicit success feedback reduces effort needed to confirm completion; normative/technique evidence, not preference proof.

citation: Sweller J. Cognitive load during problem solving: Effects on learning. Cognitive Science. 1988;12(2):257-285. doi:10.1016/0364-0213(88)90023-7
notes: Separates intrinsic from manipulable/extraneous load; expertise/schema differences matter. Does not support a generic less-information rule.

citation: Mayer RE, Moreno R. Nine ways to reduce cognitive load in multimedia learning. Educational Psychologist. 2003;38:43-52; summarized in Cambridge Handbook of Multimedia Learning.
notes: Targets extraneous processing and signaling/contiguity rather than raw information count.

citation: Pirolli P, Card SK. Information Foraging. Psychological Review. 1999;106(4):643-675. doi:10.1037/0033-295X.106.4.643
notes: People adapt strategies/environment to maximize rate of valuable information gain; supports payoff/scent framing rather than minimum-content dogma.

citation: Scheibehenne B, Greifeneder R, Todd PM. Can There Ever Be Too Many Options? Journal of Consumer Research. 2010;37(3):409-425. doi:10.1086/651235
notes: Mean choice-overload effect virtually zero with substantial heterogeneity; direct counterweight to universal fewer-options prescriptions.

citation: Greifeneder R, Scheibehenne B, Kleber N. Less may be more when choosing is difficult: Choice complexity and too much choice. Acta Psychologica. 2010;133(1):45-50. doi:10.1016/j.actpsy.2009.08.005
population_or_context: choice sets varying options and attributes
notes: Choice overload emerged when alternatives differed on many attributes, not few; supports conditional rather than universal one-action logic.

citation: Chernev A, Böckenholt U, Goodman J. Choice overload: A conceptual review and meta-analysis. Journal of Consumer Psychology. 2015;25(2):333-358. doi:10.1016/j.jcps.2014.08.002
culture_axes: choice complexity; task difficulty; preference uncertainty; decision goal
notes: Identifies moderators of when assortment size harms choice; supports explicit exploration/execution boundary.

citation: Lee JD, See KA. Trust in Automation: Designing for Appropriate Reliance. Human Factors. 2004;46(1):50-80. doi:10.1518/hfes.46.1.50_30392
claim_ids: Frames target as appropriate reliance, not maximal trust; trust and reliance depend on context and system characteristics.

citation: Hoff KA, Bashir M. Trust in automation: integrating empirical evidence on factors that influence trust. Human Factors. 2015;57(3):407-434. doi:10.1177/0018720814547570
notes: Three-layer model of trust variability; undermines treating trust as one interface-produced scalar.

citation: Hunsicker T, Duhl I, Haubert P, Onnasch L, Langer M. Trust the Explanation or my Expectation? International Journal of Human-Computer Studies. 2026;211:103775. doi:10.1016/j.ijhcs.2026.103775
notes: For inaccurate outputs, explanations increased trusting behavior; direct evidence that more explanation can worsen calibrated reliance.

citation: Customers' acceptance of artificially intelligent service robots: The influence of trust and culture. International Journal of Information Management. 2023.
notes: Culture moderated several trust/intention relationships; useful boundary evidence, not a country-level deterministic rule.

citation: Wang P, Ding H. The rationality of explanation or human capacity? Understanding the impact of explainable AI on human-AI trust and decision performance. Information Processing & Management. 2024;61(4):103732.
notes: Explanations affected behavioral reliance/accuracy differently from self-reported trust; supports separating subjective trust from behavior.

citation: Wood C et al. The Impact of Asking Intention or Self-Prediction Questions on Subsequent Behavior: A Meta-Analysis. Personality and Social Psychology Review. 2016. doi:10.1177/1088868315592334
culture_axes: behavior domain; desirability; difficulty; sample type
notes: Asking intention/self-prediction questions has a small positive effect on later behavior; measurement can be intervention.

citation: Miles LM, Rodrigues AM, Sniehotta FF, French DP. Asking questions changes health-related behavior: updated systematic review and meta-analysis. Journal of Clinical Epidemiology. 2020;123:59-68. doi:10.1016/j.jclinepi.2020.03.014
notes: Small but significant QBE with substantial heterogeneity; explicitly treats measurement reactivity as a bias risk.

citation: Development of symptom assessments utilising item response theory and computer-adaptive testing—A practical method based on a systematic review. Critical Reviews in Oncology/Hematology. 2010;73(1):47-67. doi:10.1016/j.critrevonc.2009.03.007
notes: Adaptive testing selects the most informative next item but requires calibrated item banks and subgroup equivalence; simply shortening can lose individual-level validity.

citation: Measurement precision and user experience with adaptive versus non-adaptive psychometric tests. Personality and Individual Differences. 2024;225:112675.
notes: CAT improved measurement precision with minimal UX benefit and signs of greater effort; supports information gain vs burden tradeoff.
